LESSON: THE EARLY CHURCH

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Church
Topic 5.2: The Early Church

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Early Church. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how the early church was started, • repent their sins as guided in Acts 2:38. How was the early church started?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. name the disciples of Jesus Christ
2. describe how the early church was started

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE EARLY CHURCH
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Early Church helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE EARLY CHURCH
Study The Early Church like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Name the disciples of Jesus Christ

What this means
In this part you learn to name the disciples of Jesus Christ. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name the disciples of Jesus Christ.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Early Church” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name the disciples of Jesus Christ. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how the early church was started

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how the early church was started. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how the early church was started.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Early Church in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how the early church was started. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Early Church is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Early Church” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: name the disciples of Jesus Christ)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Early Church in your own words. (skill: describe how the early church was started)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Early Church to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: name the disciples of Jesus Christ.
3. Practise this skill: describe how the early church was started.
4. Make one local Kenya example of The Early Church from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Early Church: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study The Early Church?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how the early church was started, • repent their sins as guided in Acts 2:38. How was the early church started?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Early Church means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: name the disciples of Jesus Christ.
5. Be able to: describe how the early church was started.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
